Looking at this PR carefully, I need to focus on the new `addGuests` handler (most complex logic), the permission checks, and how the new code interacts with existing booking/calendar/email flows.

      "file": "packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts",
      "line": 47,
      "severity": "critical",
      "category": "security",
      "title": "Team admin/owner permission check uses && instead of ||",
      "body": "The `isTeamAdminOrOwner` check uses `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`. In cal.com's role model these are mutually exclusive (a user is either admin OR owner), so the conjunction always evaluates to false. The code clearly intended `||`. Effect: every team admin and every team owner is treated as unauthorized and rejected with `FORBIDDEN`; only direct organizers or existing attendees can add guests to team event bookings, defeating the entire intent of this branch."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts",
      "line": 54,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "security",
      "title": "Existing attendees are allowed to add arbitrary guests",
      "body": "Permission check is `!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee -> FORBIDDEN`. Because `isAttendee` is satisfied by any existing attendee whose email matches the logged-in user's email, an invitee of a booking can invite unlimited additional people (including themselves under a different email) to that booking without the organizer's consent. This is a privilege escalation: an attendee can grow the meeting's attendee list and trigger calendar invites / emails on behalf of the organizer. At minimum, only the organizer / team admin / owner should be able to add guests."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts",
      "line": 168,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "sendAddGuestsEmails is called with unfiltered input, causing duplicate AttendeeScheduledEmail to existing attendees",
      "body": "The handler passes the original `guests` array (which may contain already-attending emails that were filtered out into `uniqueGuests`) into `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`. If an organizer re-typings an existing attendee's email by mistake, that attendee will be re-issued a brand-new booking confirmation with a fresh ICS REQUEST. The function should receive the deduplicated `uniqueGuests` (or compute the post-update set) instead."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts",
      "line": 44,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "No booking status check: guests can be added to cancelled or past bookings",
      "body": "The handler never inspects `booking.status` (or `booking.startTime`). The action item in `BookingListItem.tsx` is reachable for past confirmed bookings and any tRPC caller can bypass the UI entirely and call the mutation for a cancelled/rejected booking. Adding attendees to a cancelled booking results in an orphan calendar invite to a meeting that will not occur and may push the meeting back into an active state on connected calendars."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts",
      "line": 70,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "security",
      "title": "Case-sensitive blacklist and existing-attendee filter are trivially bypassable",
      "body": "`blacklistedGuestEmails` is lowercased but `guest` is compared as-is: `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`. An email like `BOB@example.com` bypasses the env-var blacklist. All email comparisons for guest handling should be lowercased before comparison."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts",
      "line": 92,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "Calendar sync after DB commit with no rollback: inconsistent state on failure",
      "body": "`prisma.booking.update` is executed before `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`. The calendar update is not wrapped in try/catch, so if it throws (e.g. credentials revoked, Google 5xx) the DB rows have already been inserted but the connected calendar has not been updated. A retry will then hit `uniqueGuests.length === 0` and return a misleading `emails_must_be_unique_valid` error, leaving the meeting with attendees in the DB but not on the calendar and not notified. The handler should either perform the calendar update first (with compensation on DB failure) or wrap both in a transactional pattern."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts",
      "line": 160,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "EventManager is built from the caller's credentials instead of the organizer's",
      "body": "`new EventManager({ ...user, credentials: [...credentials] })` uses the currently authenticated user's spread and credentials. When the caller is a team admin or (in the corrected logic) an attendee, the calendar invite will be pushed through whichever calendar integration the caller has, not the organizer's. That causes the organizer to lose control of the event on their primary calendar and may fail entirely if the caller has no calendar credentials for the destinationCalendar."

      "file": "packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts",

A reasonable bound (e.g. `.max(50)` or `.max(100)`) should be enforced at the schema layer to prevent abuse and keep the email/calendar blast radius small."

      "file": "packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts",

      "category": "bug",

      "severity": "low",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Subject reads attendees[0].name without guarding empty array",

      "file": "apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx",
      "line": 26,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Inline Zod schema diverges from the backend schema and validates case-sensitively",
